intro: Bring this review to the infectious disease appointment: symptoms, dated evidence and questions to work through together. It brings together infection testing and relevant findings from other specialties; it does not assign an infectious diagnosis.
scope: Selected dated findings are shown below, with links to every selected test’s full recorded history. All 32 results from 10 and 20 October are included. Older results are historical evidence, not a current clearance of infection.

highlights.title: Recent infection screen
highlights.text: September/October testing is largely negative. Hepatitis A total antibody and hepatitis B surface antibody have immunity-related interpretations, not a diagnosis of active hepatitis.

highlights.title: Possible past triggers
highlights.text: Campylobacter PCR was positive in 2017; CMV IgG was detected in 2020. COVID episodes are supported by dated personal records in May 2022 and February 2024. Causation of ongoing symptoms is unestablished.

highlights.title: Keep the timelines separate
highlights.text: Longstanding throat symptoms, nocturia and some musculoskeletal symptoms predate documented COVID episodes. Later worsening and any symptom-free intervals still need to be mapped.

symptoms.title: Soft-tissue pain
symptoms.label: Patient-reported pattern
symptoms.text: Load- or stretch-triggered pain at multiple sites, delayed finger swelling/stiffness after typing, guarding and loss of knee/elbow extension. Shoulder symptoms by about 2017; ankle symptoms by 2021; further sites accumulated during 2022–2024. Exact dates vary between retrospective notes.
symptoms.question: Does the examination suggest enthesitis or reactive arthritis, muscle disease, a post-infectious process, or separate local injuries? Which episodes have a credible time link to an infection?

symptoms.title: Throat phlegm
symptoms.label: Patient-reported since about 2017
symptoms.text: Persistent mucus and throat clearing; sometimes brown or green, aggravated by smoke/irritants and overnight dryness. Symptoms have persisted across homes and periods without smoking. ENT feedback in August 2026 is patient-reported; the original letter has not been reviewed.
symptoms.question: Is the mucus coming from the nose/throat or lower airways? Would examination and the cough pattern justify a fresh, appropriately collected sample or respiratory/ENT assessment?

symptoms.title: Nocturia
symptoms.label: Longstanding patient-reported symptom
symptoms.text: Repeated waking to void, sometimes at relatively small volumes; estimates of overnight volume vary and are not a formal diary. The September 2025 ultrasound recorded a normal urinary tract and 11 mL post-void residual. October urine chemistry does not include a bacterial culture.
symptoms.question: Is there evidence for urinary infection or prostatitis, or does a bladder diary and urinary/sleep assessment better explain the pattern? Review dysuria, pelvic pain, fever and exposure history.

symptoms.title: Gut and other symptoms
symptoms.label: Patient-reported; current status to confirm
symptoms.text: Methane-positive breath testing, constipation and gas; constipation improved after antibiotics and starting prucalopride. Notes also describe intermittent orthostatic symptoms, cold/purple extremities, flushing, itch and skin reactivity. These have no established infectious explanation.
symptoms.question: Which symptoms started or clearly worsened after an infection, and which need a separate gastrointestinal, autonomic, allergy or rheumatology assessment?

context.title: Imaging and rheumatology
context.source: Reviewed dashboard reports; left-knee report is a transcription
context.text: Right-knee MRI (September 2025): severe insertional semimembranosus tendinopathy with adjacent oedema and a small ganglion. Left-knee MRI (September 2026): mild distal muscle oedema described as strain, with normal tendon insertions. Right hand/wrist MRI (May 2026): no synovitis or tenosynovitis. Rheumatology review (November 2025) recorded no active synovitis. These findings are relevant to symptom localization; they do not identify an infectious cause.

context.title: Urinary tract ultrasound · 16 September 2025
context.source: Original report checked for this review
context.text: No renal or urinary tract abnormality identified. No hydronephrosis or renal calculi; bladder appeared normal. Pre-void volume 254 mL, post-void 11 mL (4%). Prostate volume 21 cc. Earlier notes mention a prostate calcification, which is not described in this report; no inference of prostatitis is made.

context.title: Sinus CT · 25 September 2020
context.source: Original report checked for this review
context.text: Clear paranasal sinuses, nasal passage and nasopharynx; no sinus disease demonstrated. Useful historical context, but not a current ENT assessment.

context.title: ENT assessment · 11 August 2026
context.source: Patient report in personal notes; original letter pending
context.text: Reported incomplete laryngeal/vocal-fold closure during speech, no visible reflux inflammation and a recommendation for voice therapy. Exact diagnosis and findings need confirmation from the ENT letter.

context.title: COVID and the symptom timeline
context.source: Dated personal records; no laboratory SARS-CoV-2 result in HealthDB
context.text: A May 2022 episode was contemporaneously described as COVID. February 2024 records include a positive rapid-antigen-test photo. A February 2023 illness was suspected but unconfirmed. Some pain and throat symptoms predate these episodes. A post-infectious assessment depends on the clinical timeline; no routine laboratory test definitively confirms or excludes Long COVID.

context.title: Antibiotics and response · 2026
context.source: Treatment history from personal notes; reconcile dates and doses at the appointment
context.text: Rifaximin 550 mg three times daily plus metronidazole 400 mg three times daily, recorded 7–20 May. A second course in approximately mid-to-late July also included bismuth. Constipation improved, but prucalopride began after the first course, so attribution is uncertain. The June breath retest is described as methane 11 ppm baseline / 14 ppm peak in notes; its original report has not been checked or added to HealthDB. No established durable improvement in soft-tissue pain is documented; early nocturia changes were confounded by fluid intake. Review other antibiotics, especially any fluoroquinolone exposure, and steroid use.

context.title: Bone and nutritional context
context.text: April 2026 DXA: lumbar-spine Z-score −3.0, femoral-neck −2.6, total-hip −2.0. Low bone density, low/borderline ALP and copper/caeruloplasmin history deserve their own clinical interpretation; they do not establish an infection mechanism.

questions.title: What is the leading clinical pattern?
questions.text: Ask the specialist to distinguish active infection, a reaction after infection, and non-infectious causes. Compare the 2017 Campylobacter result and later illnesses with the onset of each painful site; a positive remote test alone is insufficient.

questions.title: Which exposures change the interpretation?
questions.text: Bring travel and residence dates, tick/mosquito bites, livestock or animal-birth exposure, soil/freshwater exposure, TB contacts and relevant sexual exposure timing. Review vaccinations and antibiotics or steroids around each test. Missing exposure information is not the same as no exposure.

questions.title: Which sample would answer the current symptom?
questions.text: For phlegm, clarify nasal drainage versus sputum and the presence of persistent cough, breathlessness or fever. For urinary symptoms, clarify dysuria, pelvic/perineal pain, discharge or fever. Ask whether targeted culture/PCR or another specialty assessment is warranted by the examination, rather than repeating the entire screen.

questions.title: What needs documenting before follow-up?
questions.text: Bring a short symptom timeline, a three-day frequency/volume and fluid diary, medication courses and response, the ENT letter and original June breath-test report. Record whether there have been recurrent measured fevers, drenching night sweats, weight loss, swollen glands, rash or eye inflammation; these are not reliably documented as present or absent in the reviewed material.

notes: This is a curated appointment review of the available records, not an exhaustive list of every possible infectious cause or a recommendation to order every test.

Dates are the dates stored in HealthDB unless a collection/report distinction is explicitly stated. Laboratory labels are anonymised. Original private pathology PDFs are retained locally, not attached to this public dashboard.
Patient observations, clinician/report findings and discussion questions are labelled separately. Explanatory theories in personal notes have not been promoted to diagnoses.

Selected results use the current lab snapshot. October source comments and thresholds were checked against the reports. Other stored bounds are shown as bounds, without inventing inclusive/exclusive limits.

No current routine bacterial urine culture or current lower-airway sputum culture was found in the reviewed HealthDB results. This is a record gap, not proof that no such testing has ever been performed.
